summary: Triptorelin is a synthetic decapeptide GnRH agonist given as a long-acting intramuscular depot for palliative treatment of advanced prostate cancer. Continuous (rather than pulsatile) GnRH receptor stimulation initially raises, then suppresses, LH/FSH and testosterone to castrate levels. An early testosterone surge can cause transient tumor flare. Important risks include tumor flare, metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular events, and rare anaphylaxis.
indications: Palliative treatment of advanced prostate cancer (androgen deprivation therapy)

dosage.n: Depot strengths are not additive - select by dosing schedule

admin: Administer under the supervision of a physician as a single intramuscular injection into either buttock
Reconstitute the lyophilized microgranules only with the provided sterile water; use no other diluent
Administer the suspension within 2 minutes of reconstitution
Rotate the injection site; depot strengths are not interchangeable on a milligram basis
moa: Triptorelin is a synthetic decapeptide agonist analogue of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) with much greater potency than native GnRH. Initial administration stimulates the pituitary to release LH and FSH, transiently increasing testosterone. With continuous (non-pulsatile) exposure, pituitary GnRH receptors are downregulated and desensitized, suppressing LH/FSH secretion and reducing testosterone to castrate levels, producing medical castration that deprives androgen-dependent prostate cancer of its hormonal stimulus.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to triptorelin, any product component, other GnRH agonists, or GnRH itself
relative: Metastatic vertebral lesions or urinary tract obstruction (flare may cause spinal cord compression/obstruction)
Pre-existing cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or metabolic syndrome
Low bone mineral density / osteoporosis risk

preg: Triptorelin for advanced prostate cancer is used in men. GnRH agonists are contraindicated in pregnancy and can cause fetal harm; this product is not indicated in women.
lact: Not applicable - the indicated population (advanced prostate cancer) is men.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is defined; the depot formulation does not lend itself to adjustment. Exposure may be higher in renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is defined. Exposure may be higher in hepatic impairment.

major: QT-prolonging drugs / antiarrhythmics (additive QT prolongation risk with androgen deprivation)
moderate: Drugs affecting serum prolactin (may reduce GnRH receptor expression)
Antihyperglycemic agents (androgen deprivation can worsen glycemic control)
interactions.diagnostics: Suppresses pituitary-gonadal axis - interferes with diagnostic tests of pituitary gonadotropic and gonadal function during and after therapy; alters testosterone and PSA

serious: Tumor flare (worsening symptoms, spinal cord compression, urinary obstruction) early in therapy
Cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, sudden cardiac death, stroke)
emergency: Symptoms of spinal cord compression (leg weakness, sensory loss, bladder/bowel dysfunction)

monitoring: Serum testosterone and PSA to confirm and follow androgen suppression
Blood glucose/HbA1c and lipid profile (metabolic syndrome)
Cardiovascular status; consider ECG/electrolytes for QT risk
Bone mineral density over long-term therapy
Symptoms of tumor flare in the first weeks
counsel: Symptoms may briefly worsen (bone pain, urinary symptoms) in the first weeks before improving - report severe back/leg weakness or trouble urinating right away
Hot flushes, reduced sex drive, and fatigue are common with androgen deprivation
Keep all scheduled injection appointments to maintain effect
Long-term therapy can affect blood sugar, cholesterol, bone strength, and the heart - these will be monitored
Report chest pain, severe headache, or signs of an allergic reaction immediately
pk: Initial gonadotropin/testosterone surge within days; suppression to castrate testosterone within about 2-4 weeks
Peak triptorelin concentration shortly after IM injection, then sustained depot release
Terminal half-life in the range of several hours for the peptide; effect sustained by depot release over the dosing interval
4, 12, or 24 weeks depending on depot strength
Store at controlled room temperature; reconstitute immediately before use
pearls: Continuous GnRH agonism downregulates pituitary receptors, producing medical castration after an initial flare
Antiandrogen pretreatment is often used to blunt the early testosterone surge (tumor flare), especially with high tumor burden
Depot strengths (3.75/11.25/22.5 mg) are not additive - choose by the intended dosing interval
Androgen deprivation increases cardiometabolic and fracture risk - monitor and counsel
Confirm castrate testosterone if PSA fails to fall as expected
missed: Triptorelin depot is given on a fixed schedule (every 4, 12, or 24 weeks) by a healthcare provider. If an injection appointment is missed, contact the clinic to reschedule as soon as possible to maintain testosterone suppression; do not skip doses.
overdose: Overdose experience is limited; because of the depot formulation, accidental over-administration is unlikely. Manage symptomatically and supportively. There is no specific antidote; effects relate to exaggerated hormonal suppression and would resolve as the depot is cleared.
